SMTO-TSK-0061 — SMTO can't read which tasks this task waits for

GUID: ad6592d9-51f5-4d01-aff6-69431985b967
Slug: task-dependency-store-invalid
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • SMTO saves a note of which earlier task each task waits for. That note is damaged for this task, so SMTO won't start it rather than guess the order.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Select Copy error details and note which conversation and task showed this message. The person fixing it needs to know exactly which task's saved order is damaged.
  2. Send the copied details to the person who installed or manages SMTO. The error alone does not establish a repair you can safely do yourself; fixing saved task data needs their tools.
  3. Until it's fixed, avoid deleting this task or the tasks around it in the conversation. Those tasks hold the history needed to repair the order correctly.

What success looks like

  • After the repair, the task shows a normal status such as Queued, Waiting for dependency or Running instead of this error.

If it still fails

  • If the person managing SMTO needs more, send them the Server log from around the time of the error. Don't delete SMTO's data folder or remove the task's waiting order to force it to run.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A task record's stored dependencies_json decoded to a value that is not a list ("Invalid persisted dependency array"), so the task store refused to treat it as having no dependencies.

What this means

  • Persisted dependencies_json decodes/thaws to a value other than a list; item schema parsing may separately reject malformed edges. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • Persisted dependencies_json decodes/thaws to a value other than a list; item schema parsing may separately reject malformed edges.

How to diagnose it

  • Preserve the original task record and inspect its supported stored schema instead of treating unreadable links as no dependencies.

How to fix it

  • Back up the task store, then inspect the affected agent_tasks row's dependencies_json (it must be a JSON array of TaskDependency objects) and find how it was written. Repair it only through supported repair or migration tooling and keep the Error ID for a bug report; do not clear the dependencies to force the task to run.
  • Preserve the task store and inspect the affected task through supported repair/migration tooling. Do not discard dependencies to force execution.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Supported repair/migration restores a valid dependency list without losing ordering requirements.

What not to do

  • Do not delete evidence or invent a configuration change for an unexplained internal failure.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
